assumptions.choice: Size each entry so stop-loss distance risks exactly 1% of current portfolio value (shares = 1% equity / per-share risk).
assumptions.reason: Spec explicitly recommends fixed risk per trade of 1-2% tied to the stop-loss distance; picked the lower end of the stated range as a single concrete value.

assumptions.choice: TP = entry +/- 2x the stop-loss distance (1:2 risk:reward).
assumptions.reason: This value is given verbatim in the spec as its own recommended default.

assumptions.choice: Post-breakout price must extend at least 25% of the OR range beyond the breakout boundary before the pullback/Fibonacci search begins; if price falls back inside the range first, the setup is invalidated.
assumptions.reason: Spec requires a 'strong move (impulse)' but gives no numeric threshold; a modest fraction of the OR range was chosen as a literal, minimal quantification.

assumptions.choice: The retracement swing runs from the breakout boundary (OR High for longs / OR Low for shorts) to the extreme price reached during the confirmed impulse.
assumptions.reason: Spec says Fibonacci is 'applied to the price move after the range breakout,' i.e., the impulse leg; anchoring at the breakout boundary is the most literal reading.

assumptions.choice: Current 1-minute close higher than the prior close (long) / lower than the prior close (short) while price sits in the 50-61.8% golden zone.
assumptions.reason: Spec says price should show 'signs of a reversal' without naming an indicator or pattern; used the simplest directional tick as a literal proxy.

assumptions.choice: Manually aggregated 1-hour bars (built from the single 1-minute feed) with SMA(50) of hourly closes; uptrend if last hourly close > SMA50, downtrend if below.
assumptions.reason: Spec offers '1-hour or 4-hour' as an example; chose 1-hour, the shorter cited option, and built it manually since the harness supplies only a single 1-minute PandasData feed with no cerebro-level resampling available to the strategy.

assumptions.choice: Implemented SMA(50) of 1-hour closes exactly as specified, even though the ~6.5-day, 2516-bar 1-minute feed yields at most ~39 hourly closes -- short of 50 -- so the trend filter may stay unset (None) for the whole run, blocking all entries.
assumptions.reason: A true 50-period 1-hour SMA needs roughly 50 trading hours (~8 sessions) of history, more than this environment's fixed data window provides; per the rules, the literal parameter (50) was kept rather than shrinking it to force trades.

assumptions.choice: A new session is detected via a change in the bar's date; Opening Range, breakout state, and Fibonacci levels reset every new day, while the hourly-close history feeding the trend SMA is not reset and stays continuous across sessions.
assumptions.reason: The OR is explicitly a 'first trading hour' (daily) concept, but the higher-timeframe trend indicator is conventionally continuous market context.

assumptions.choice: After any exit (stop-loss, take-profit, or alternative in-range exit) the day's breakout/impulse/Fibonacci state is cleared, allowing a fresh 15-minute breakout to be sought again later the same session rather than disabling trading for the rest of the day.
assumptions.reason: Spec states no one-trade-per-day limit; canonical default #3 only forbids concurrent positions, so sequential re-entries after going flat are the more literal reading.

assumptions.choice: Stop is placed exactly at OR Low (long) / OR High (short) with no buffer; the alternative exit fires as soon as Close crosses back past that same boundary (OR High for longs, OR Low for shorts).
assumptions.reason: Literal reading of 'placed below/above the boundary' and 'full return of the price back inside the initial range.'
